cell_line: The cell line HFF-1 (SCRC-1041; ATCC, Manassas, VA, USA) was grown in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) with GlutaMAX Supplement (Gibco; Invitrogen; Thermo Fisher Scientific, Inc., Waltham, MA, USA) supplemented with 10% heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum (FBS; Gibco; Invitrogen; Thermo Fisher Scientific, Inc., Waltham, MA, USA).
cell_type: Human foreskin fibroblasts (HFF) were used as host cells to maintain T. gondii.
developmental_stage: We analyzed the type I strain RHΔHx, referred to here as RH, maintained by sequential passages through in vitro culture, and used it to obtain MOB1 recombinant protein-expressing strains.
disease_state: inferred: This study uncovers new features of the T. gondii biology, a zoonotic parasite and model organism for the phylum Apicomplexa, and highlights the complex roles MOB1 proteins may assume, with possible implications for disease processes.
material_type: We analyzed the type I strain RHΔHx, referred to here as RH, maintained by sequential passages through in vitro culture, and used it to obtain MOB1 recombinant protein-expressing strains.
sample_source: The frozen agarose beads were analyzed through mass-spectrometry by the i3S Proteomics Scientific Platform (Porto, Portugal).
species: Here, we report the identification of one MOB1 protein in the apicomplexan Toxoplasma gondii.
strain: We analyzed the type I strain RHΔHx, referred to here as RH, maintained by sequential passages through in vitro culture, and used it to obtain MOB1 recombinant protein-expressing strains.
